summary: Manage brands. A brand has websites, socials, locations and more; each holds its own tools (a website holds its SEO and Search Console). Roll-ups, research tools, connections and publishing span every brand.

brandSwitcher.note: Shows the picked brand (name from /marketing/brands/[brandId]); every "brand" section below uses that brand. With no brand picked, only the Brands section and the cross-brand sections show.

sections.name: Marketing home
sections.why: Headline numbers across brands, recent brands, and a map of everything in Marketing.

sections.name: Brands
sections.why: Every brand as cards or a table; add a brand with Smart Add.

sections.name: Brand overview
sections.why: One brand at a glance, its inbox and analytics.

sections.name: Websites
sections.why: A brand's websites; each website holds its pages, crawls, sitemaps, SEO, Search Console, content plan and reputation.

sections.name: Socials
sections.why: A brand's social accounts and the tools inside: look up, studio, outliers, swipe file, videos, ad library, KPIs.

sections.name: Locations
sections.why: A brand's locations, listings and local rank grid.

sections.name: Identity
sections.why: Who the brand is: voice, strategy, audience, claims, media, products & services.

sections.name: Outreach
sections.why: Press room, outreach, PR calendar, email and advertising.

sections.name: Competitors & monitoring
sections.why: Competitors, news monitors and what AI says about the brand.

sections.name: Reports
sections.why: Roll-ups across brands; every row opens into its brand.

sections.name: Research tools
sections.why: Analyzers and research that need no brand.

sections.name: Operations
sections.why: Connections, automations, approvals, capabilities, data quality.

sections.name: Publish
sections.why: CMS sites, HTML pages, podcasts and artifacts.
